katas.title: PO approval: drop the "redundant" status filter from the approve write

provenance.find: 3. **Double approval races and illegal transitions return 500.**

edits.replace:
// status was already checked by assertPurchaseOrderStatusTransition above
  await repo.approve({ id: purchaseOrderId, tenantId: session.tenantId }, session.userId);

defects.scenario: Two approvers click Approve on the same PENDING_APPROVAL purchase order at the same moment; both requests read the row before either writes.
defects.find: await repo.approve({ id: purchaseOrderId, tenantId: session.tenantId }, session.userId);
defects.consequence: The status check now happens only in JavaScript on a stale read; the write no longer re-checks PENDING_APPROVAL, so both requests succeed, two purchaseOrder.approved audit rows are written and approvedById is whoever wrote last (check-then-act race).

defects.scenario: The shipped repository already writes without the status in the where clause.
defects.consequence: This is the live double-approval race the guide documents (purchaseOrderService.ts:125 read -> :134 write); the patch removes the fix instead of applying it.

tests.name: two concurrent approvals: exactly one succeeds, the other is a 409
tests.code: const rows = [{ id: 'po1', tenantId: 't1', status: 'PENDING_APPROVAL', requestedById: 'req' }]; const repo = mod.createRepository(rows, { yieldBetween: true }); const r = await Promise.allSettled([mod.approvePurchaseOrder(repo, { tenantId: 't1', userId: 'a1' }, 'po1'), mod.approvePurchaseOrder(repo, { tenantId: 't1', userId: 'a2' }, 'po1')]); assert.equal(r.filter((x) => x.status === 'fulfilled').length, 1); const rej = r.find((x) => x.status === 'rejected'); assert.ok(rej, 'second approval must be rejected'); assert.equal(rej.reason.statusCode, 409); assert.equal(repo.audit.length, 1);

tests.name: a sequential second approval is a 409 conflict
tests.code: const rows = [{ id: 'po1', tenantId: 't1', status: 'PENDING_APPROVAL', requestedById: 'req' }]; const repo = mod.createRepository(rows); await mod.approvePurchaseOrder(repo, { tenantId: 't1', userId: 'a1' }, 'po1'); await assert.rejects(mod.approvePurchaseOrder(repo, { tenantId: 't1', userId: 'a2' }, 'po1'), (e) => e.statusCode === 409);

katas.title: PO approval: let admins fast-track their own purchase orders

defects.scenario: An ADMIN raises a purchase order for a vendor they control and then approves it themselves.
defects.consequence: Segregation of duties is gone for exactly the most powerful role: the requester is also the approver, so a single person can commit company spend with no second pair of eyes.

defects.scenario: The shipped approve flow has no requester check at all.
defects.consequence: The only guard before the write is the transition map (finding 1, "Self-approval is allowed"); the patch re-opens the hole the fix closed, for admins.

tests.name: an admin cannot approve a purchase order they requested
tests.code: const rows = [{ id: 'po1', tenantId: 't1', status: 'PENDING_APPROVAL', requestedById: 'boss' }]; const repo = mod.createRepository(rows); await assert.rejects(mod.approvePurchaseOrder(repo, { tenantId: 't1', userId: 'boss', role: 'ADMIN' }, 'po1'), (e) => e.statusCode === 403); assert.equal(rows[0].status, 'PENDING_APPROVAL');

tests.name: a different approver can approve
tests.code: const rows = [{ id: 'po1', tenantId: 't1', status: 'PENDING_APPROVAL', requestedById: 'boss' }]; const repo = mod.createRepository(rows); const r = await mod.approvePurchaseOrder(repo, { tenantId: 't1', userId: 'fin', role: 'APPROVER' }, 'po1'); assert.equal(r.status, 'APPROVED');

tests.name: allows approval before receiving (ported from src/test/purchase-order-transition.test.ts)
tests.code: assert.equal(mod.assertPurchaseOrderStatusTransition('PENDING_APPROVAL', 'APPROVED'), true); assert.throws(() => mod.assertPurchaseOrderStatusTransition('DRAFT', 'RECEIVED'), /Invalid purchase order transition from DRAFT to RECEIVED/);
